findings.title: Compare stored login eligibility rather than organization-aware enabled state
findings.body: The original model passed here comes from getById(), which wraps isEnabled() to return false when its organization is disabled (or organizations are disabled for the realm). The login query, however, selects IDs using the stored enabled flag. If a public, enabled organization IdP is already cached, its organization is disabled, and the IdP is then made hidden-on-login or link-only, both predicates here return false and invalidation is skipped. Re-enabling the organization leaves that IdP in the login cache; OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), so it displays the now-hidden or link-only provider. Compare the original persisted eligibility flags without the organization-aware wrapper when deciding whether query membership changed.

findings.title: Do not merge an old query after a concurrent invalidation
findings.body: When an organization search is missing, this branch carries all results from the previously read query into a replacement tagged with a freshly obtained revision and current counter. A concurrent transaction can change an IdP's login eligibility or organization and invalidate the login cache after this request reads query but before invalidateObject() runs. The replacement then reinstates the old organization's stale ID set under the new revision, even though only the newly requested organization's results were reloaded. Subsequent logins can omit newly eligible providers or display hidden/link-only providers until another invalidation. Rebuild without the old query when its revision is no longer current, and ensure a concurrent invalidation cannot be bypassed by stamping stale results with the current counter.

findings.title: Register cleanup for the actual provider alias
findings.body: The new test registers every cleanup against the literal alias "alias", rather than the provider it just created ("idp-alias-0" through "idp-alias-19"). The additional registration at line 425 has the same problem for "idp-alias-20". Cleanup therefore attempts to delete a nonexistent provider and leaves the created providers behind, including realm-level providers that organization deletion cannot clean up. This can cause cleanup failures and contaminate later tests. Capture and use each created provider's actual alias.
